subject: Post-demo: embeddings + reranker architecture — steady-state autoscale plan

Subject: Post-demo: embeddings + reranker architecture — steady-state autoscale plan

Thanks again for the afternoon demo — great discussion. I wanted to capture the engineering follow-ups we agreed on and a proposed steady-state autoscale approach so your ops team can validate assumptions. High level summary first, then a few clarifying questions we need to finalize sizing: 

Summary of the ask (from demo):
- Use-case: realtime recommendation feed ranking with a reranker stage — client generates a candidate set (top 50) and asks Redwood to produce dense embeddings + reranker scoring for final top 5.
- Latency SLO: 95th <= 180ms for reranker step end-to-end (Redwood output to your app).
- Expected steady-state: ~120 QPS average, spikes to 600 QPS for 3-5 minute bursts, peak sustained (rare) 1.2k QPS for <10 minutes during batch recompute windows.

Immediate engineering clarifications we need from FintechX before our sizing: 
1) Payload sizes: typical candidate set size (avg tokens per candidate + metadata) and whether you will send full text per candidate or only ids and ask us to fetch embeddings from your vector store.
2) Reranker complexity: are you looking for a lightweight MLP scorer (single forward pass per candidate) vs. cross-attention reranker (much heavier, not an embeddings-only flow)?
3) Auth preference for Private/Dedicated: API keys + IP allowlist, or mTLS? You mentioned stricter controls — want to confirm.
4) Failure/fallback: should Redwood fallback to hosted model variant or return an error to your service on model timeouts?

Proposed steady-state architecture (Redwood recommendation):
- Dedicated capacity pool sized for 25% headroom above steady-state average with autoscale to handle short spikes using burst tokens. For your numbers that maps to a base reservation for ~160 QPS with autoscale targetable to ~700 QPS.
- Concurrency limits: cap concurrent in-flight tokens per GPU to avoid KV cache thrash; recommend 256 concurrent streams per GPU for embedding-only workflows, 96 for cross-attention rerankers.
- Queues: introduce a two-lane queue in front of the cluster — low-latency lane (priority) for requests where client sets priority header; standard lane for background scoring. Queue depth per lane configurable, start with 2s max queuing (estimated queue size = QPS * 2s).
- Caching: enable prefix/KV cache for hot item embeddings and optional local LRU vector cache in your app to avoid repeat embedding calls.

Attachments: demo deck attached + we flagged where in the deck we show latency/cost tradeoffs.

Next steps (proposed):
- FintechX provides answers to the 4 clarifying questions and the traffic spreadsheet (if available) — we can then run a detailed queue/sizing model.
- Schedule a 90-min technical workshop (Redwood infra + FintechX backend + your SRE) — propose Wed 10/27 or Thu 10/28.
- Draft contract addendum for dedicated pool sizing (draft ready once traffic sheet + auth requirements confirmed).

Thanks — I’ll loop Ben/Logan for the deep-ops follow-up.

—

Adding a few technical notes from an ops/runtime perspective — I sketched numbers off Alyssa's CSV and Soojin's assumptions.

1) Sizing math (very rough):
- If average request includes 50 candidates * 250 bytes = ~12.5KB payload. Embedding generation per candidate (if needed) is cheap if using fast vectorizers; cross-attention reranker is the dominant cost.
- Baseline: plan for 2x CPU/GPU headroom for steady-state since reranker cross-attention has unstable seq lengths; that maps to ~4 dedicated V100-equivalent GPUs for the base 160 QPS reservation, autoscale pool to 16 GPUs for 700-1200 QPS bursts. We'll refine with workshop inputs.

2) Concurrency and queues:
- Recommend per-GPU concurrency cap of 96 for reranker flows. That yields predictable token throughput and prevents large KV cache eviction cycles.
- Queue depth: start conservative with max queueing time 1.5s for low-latency lane, 5s for background lane. We'll measure tail latency during canary to adjust.

3) Embeddings vs fetch-from-store:
- Since FintechX will likely have candidate ids, prefer fetch-from-store model: your app fetches embeddings for candidates and sends dense vectors for reranker. This reduces per-request compute and allows us to treat reranker as a pure scorer (lower cost).
- If you need us to generate embeddings, we'll treat that as an additional step — easier in a batched background job.

4) Caching strategy:
- Enable KV cache for common prefixes and a short-lived LRU vector cache in the dedicated pool for hot vectors. Helps during burst windows.

5) Observability:
- We'll surface token-level cost and per-route P95/P99 latency. For your compliance needs we can enable audit logs and payload redaction.

Attachment: queue-modeling.xlsx (workbook with baseline GPU math and queue depth sensitivity).
